instructions.note: The agent may look up any customer by email or account id supplied in the ticket, not limited to the requester's own account.
The sole stated protection against cross-customer disclosure is a prompt instruction, with no structural enforcement.
Human review is triggered only by the model's own judgment of whether the customer is "angry", an ambiguous, manipulable criterion rather than a structural approval gate.

controls.name: Prompt rule: never share another customer's information
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model choosing to follow a single-line instruction; a more capable or adversarially prompted model can rationalize exceptions or be convinced the requester is entitled to the data (ASI01).

controls.name: Requester identity binding for CRM lookups
Recipient confirmation bound to account record
Least-privilege scoped credentials for CRM and mail
Human approval gate for sends outside the verified contact
Per-run/day rate or step limit on lookups and sends

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1) with confused deputy: unrestricted CRM lookups plus a shared, unscoped send credential let any emailer exfiltrate another customer's data

attack_path.note: Untrusted customer email specifies an email or account id to look up (prompt.md:2-3 permits looking up any customer).
get_customer reads the specified account's confidential record using a broad, shared CRM_SVC_TOKEN.
The agent sends the drafted response, which can include that record's details, back to the requester's address using a shared MAIL_SVC_TOKEN that can send to any address, with no human approval.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Model/version string change in deployment config (subject.model.swappable=true, upgraded with the platform with no separate review), or any raise of step/runtime limits.

evidence.observation: States the agent may look up any customer by email or account id supplied in the ticket, without verifying it matches the sender's own identity.
Routine tickets are answered and sent directly with no human approval step; escalation depends only on the model judging the customer as angry.
The only stated control against cross-customer disclosure is a prompt instruction, not a structural restriction.
crm_mcp and mail_mcp are both called with static bearer tokens (CRM_SVC_TOKEN, MAIL_SVC_TOKEN).
CRM_SVC_TOKEN can read every customer record; MAIL_SVC_TOKEN is a shared service account that can send to any address.

recommendations.action: Verify the ticket requester's identity (e.g., match the authenticated inbound sender address against the account on file) before allowing get_customer to look up any account other than the requester's own.
Bind cap.email_send's recipient to the verified contact address on file for the matched account rather than to any address found in the request or drafted by the model.
Replace the broad CRM_SVC_TOKEN and shared MAIL_SVC_TOKEN with least-privilege, per-session scoped credentials.
Add a human approval gate (raw action review, low volume) for any send to a recipient other than the verified account contact, or that includes another account's data.

findings.title: No spend, rate, or step limit on autonomous CRM lookups and email sends

forecast.watch_signal: Median tickets processed per run or per day rising without a corresponding cap being added.

evidence.observation: No per-run or per-day cap on CRM lookups or outbound sends is described.
The agent processes each new ticket and sends routine responses directly; autonomy fields such as max_unattended_steps or max_runtime_minutes are not declared anywhere in the artifacts.

recommendations.action: Set an explicit per-run/per-day cap on get_customer lookups and email sends (max_unattended_steps, rate limit) for the agent.

stride_coverage.rationale: Artifacts do not describe how the agent authenticates itself to crm_mcp/mail_mcp beyond the shared bearer tokens, so whether the agent process can be impersonated is not assessed.
No information on whether the deployed system prompt or agent configuration can be altered without review, aside from the stated model-swap process.
Every outbound email is logged to the SIEM, giving a record of the agent's send actions.
Unrestricted lookups plus unrestricted sends let the agent disclose any customer's data to any requester.
No step, rate, or spend limit is declared on the agent's loop.
The agent acts with broad shared-service credentials exceeding what an individual requester is entitled to.
The sender's claimed identity (email/account id in the ticket) is not verified against the authenticated channel before CRM lookups proceed.
The external sender is outside the organization's systems; non-repudiation of their claims is not a property this agent's internal controls can provide.
Artifacts do not describe transport integrity protections for inbound email ingestion into the agent.
Artifacts do not describe whether inbound email content is encrypted or who can read it in transit or storage.
A flood of inbound tickets has no stated limit on how many lookups/sends the agent will perform in response.
Artifacts do not describe integrity protection on the call to mail_mcp.send.
This is the egress channel through which another customer's confidential data can be sent to the requester.
No cap on the volume of outbound sends is declared.
mcp.json shows only a static bearer token for crm_mcp; whether server identity is verified beyond HTTPS/TLS is not stated.
Tool/definition pinning for crm_mcp (definitions_pinned) is not stated in mcp.json.
No mention of CRM-side read audit logging separate from the SIEM email log.
get_customer can read any account's confidential record given only an email or account id from the ticket.
No rate limit on CRM reads is declared.
CRM_SVC_TOKEN grants read access to every customer record regardless of which customer is asking.
mcp.json shows only a static bearer token for mail_mcp; server identity verification beyond HTTPS/TLS is not stated.
Tool/definition pinning for mail_mcp is not stated in mcp.json.
Runtime notes state every outbound email is logged to the SIEM.
mail_mcp.send can deliver confidential CRM data to any address the agent chooses.
No rate or volume limit on sends is declared.
MAIL_SVC_TOKEN is a shared service account that can send to any address, beyond what any single requester should control.
The agent's only declared CRM capability is get_customer (read); no write or delete action on CRM records is exposed, so this store cannot be tampered via this agent's capability set.
The store can be read in full for any account via the unrestricted get_customer lookup.
No read-rate limit on the store is declared.
The agent has no declared capability to write, delete, or configure SIEM records; tampering by the agent is not possible given its capability set.
Access controls on who can view SIEM-logged email content, which may include customer data, are not described.
No information on SIEM log capacity, retention, or availability guarantees is given.
Logging every outbound email to the SIEM provides an attributable record of send actions.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is critical: an untrusted customer email can direct a read of any customer's confidential record via a broad, shared CRM credential, then an autonomous send to any address via a broad, shared mail credential, with no human approval gate (lethal trifecta plus confused deputy, finding-1). The only present control is a single prompt instruction (dependent, behavioral), which credits one tier down to a high residual. Because that instruction is the sole safeguard and the model is upgraded with the platform without separate review (subject.model.swappable=true), model_upgrade and longer_task_horizon are expected to erode it, returning the forecast to critical. A secondary property finding (finding-2) notes the absence of any volume, rate, or step limit on lookups and sends, independently rated high and unaffected by those triggers since no control currently covers it.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md, mcp.json, and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.

No tool manifest or MCP schema for get_customer/send was provided; exact capability scope (e.g., whether get_customer truly accepts arbitrary account ids as prompt.md states) is inferred, so confidence is medium.
No information on peer identity verification or tool definition pinning for crm_mcp/mail_mcp was provided; the relevant stride_coverage entries are marked not_assessed.
No declared max_unattended_steps, max_runtime_minutes, or rate/spend limits were found; these are treated as absent rather than assumed to exist.
